devdoc.details: This contract implements a proxy that is upgradeable by an admin. To avoid https://medium.com/nomic-labs-blog/malicious-backdoors-in-ethereum-proxies-62629adf3357[proxy selector clashing], which can potentially be used in an attack, this contract uses the https://blog.openzeppelin.com/the-transparent-proxy-pattern/[transparent proxy pattern]. This pattern implies two things that go hand in hand: 1. If any account other than the admin calls the proxy, the call will be forwarded to the implementation, even if that call matches one of the admin functions exposed by the proxy itself. 2. If the admin calls the proxy, it can access the admin functions, but its calls will never be forwarded to the implementation. If the admin tries to call a function on the implementation it will fail with an error that says "admin cannot fallback to proxy target". These properties mean that the admin account can only be used for admin actions like upgrading the proxy or changing the admin, so it's best if it's a dedicated account that is not used for anything else. This will avoid headaches due to sudden errors when trying to call a function from the proxy implementation. Our recommendation is for the dedicated account to be an instance of the {ProxyAdmin} contract. If set up this way, you should think of the `ProxyAdmin` instance as the real administrative interface of your proxy. NOTE: The real interface of this proxy is that defined in `ITransparentUpgradeableProxy`. This contract does not inherit from that interface, and instead the admin functions are implicitly implemented using a custom dispatch mechanism in `_fallback`. Consequently, the compiler will not produce an ABI for this contract. This is necessary to fully implement transparency without decoding reverts caused by selector clashes between the proxy and the implementation. WARNING: It is not recommended to extend this contract to add additional external functions. If you do so, the compiler will not check that there are no selector conflicts, due to the note above. A selector clash between any new function and the functions declared in {ITransparentUpgradeableProxy} will be resolved in favor of the new one. This could render the admin operations inaccessible, which could prevent upgradeability. Transparency may also be compromised.

approve(address,uint256).details: See {IERC20-approve}. NOTE: If `amount` is the maximum `uint256`, the allowance is not updated on `transferFrom`. This is semantically equivalent to an infinite approval. Requirements: - `spender` cannot be the zero address.

decimals().details: Decimals are computed by adding the decimal offset on top of the underlying asset's decimals. This "original" value is cached during construction of the vault contract. If this read operation fails (e.g., the asset has not been created yet), a default of 18 is used to represent the underlying asset's decimals. See {IERC20Metadata-decimals}.

decreaseAllowance(address,uint256).details: Atomically decreases the allowance granted to `spender` by the caller. This is an alternative to {approve} that can be used as a mitigation for problems described in {IERC20-approve}. Emits an {Approval} event indicating the updated allowance. Requirements: - `spender` cannot be the zero address. - `spender` must have allowance for the caller of at least `subtractedValue`.

deposit(uint256,address).details: Same function as in ERC4626 but removes maxDeposit check and add validDeposit modifier who checks for minDeposit

depositETH(address).details: Equivalent to deposit function but for native token

getRoleAdmin(bytes32).details: Returns the admin role that controls `role`. See {grantRole} and {revokeRole}. To change a role's admin, use {_setRoleAdmin}.

grantRole(bytes32,address).details: Grants `role` to `account`. If `account` had not been already granted `role`, emits a {RoleGranted} event. Requirements: - the caller must have ``role``'s admin role. May emit a {RoleGranted} event.

increaseAllowance(address,uint256).details: Atomically increases the allowance granted to `spender` by the caller. This is an alternative to {approve} that can be used as a mitigation for problems described in {IERC20-approve}. Emits an {Approval} event indicating the updated allowance. Requirements: - `spender` cannot be the zero address.

Stake $ETH for rewards and still have access to your assets with a liquid staking token from Meta Pool. This innovative solution enhances the functionality of the $ETH token by offering a staking service that allows users to earn rewards while their tokens remain liquid and accessible. ## What is $spETH? spETH is a yield bearing asset, **accruing in value every second** meaning that you keep earning staking rewards, while you can use spETH for DeFi (coming soon) on Ethereum Network. ### Benefit of Liquid staking with Meta Pool in ETH * **spETH accruing in value every second.** * Liquid staking in Meta Pool allows users to stake small amounts of ETH (min. 0.01 ETH) instead of requiring 32 ETH which is needed to run a validator node on the Ethereum Network. * Ethereum's staking rewards primarily come from two sources: **Block Rewards + Transaction Fees.** * Fast Unstake. When you stake with Meta Pool you have the option to **access ETH immediately** (Liquid Unstaking) by paying a small fee (starting at 0.25%) ## Liquidity Pool (LP) For the purpose of enabling fast unstaking for spETH holders, Meta Pool includes an spETH / ETH liquidity pool. Users providing liquidity to the spETH<*>ETH* liquidity pool can earn fees on each fast unstake. The spETH<*>ETH* Liquidity Pool is a single token AMM. Liquidity providers add only ETH to the liquidity pool. The pool allows other users to perform "Fast Unstakes". During a "Fast Unstake" users send spETH and receive ETH from the liquidity pool, minus a fee. ## True price All spETH is backed by staked ETH in validators. The protocol is sound in the sense that it can be wind down, meaning all spETH can be burned, validators shut down and the recovered ETH + rewards will be made available to the original spETH owners. Considering that all spETH is fully backed by ETH, there's a "true price" for spETH and that's the share price of the ERC-4626 standard the Meta Pool contract implements. If you need to obtain the true price for spETH/ETH, you need to call the ERC-4626 standard function \`convertToAssets(1000000000000000000)\` This true price is the one used at all times, in fast-unstake operations and also in delayed-unstake operations. ## Delayed Unstake Delayed unstake operations have no fee, thus honoring the true price, but since it could be required to exit validators in order to make the ETH available, a delayed unstake operation may require from 7 to 14 days in order to be completed

This is current Ethereum spETH 0xD06f6a56c5f599cB375B616DF306f32B7F6f4A0E, not compromised legacy mpETH. Current primary deployment and product docs advertise normal ETH staking plus fast and delayed unstaking; current source initialize explicitly replaces balances from the June 17, 2025 incident. No recovery distribution or legacy mint method is admitted. Documentation is normal-product lifecycle evidence, not a new audit, safety assurance or a claim about incident reimbursement.

Current EIP1967 source-service resolution identifies staking implementation 0xD3dB79D2D00A6B82531D8Ccf65C376d9eE9513aC, withdrawal implementation 0xcB894c063c74053c9401ac8FDd9A9f2bb1a03c61 and liquid pool implementation 0xeA9fec1ff24B523424F21eeA5c249f9b29A1AA81. Exact source-service match labels are retained, including non-exact match for Withdrawal implementation. All are upgradeable, and staking admin may change withdrawal and pool dependencies; no persistent implementation binding is implied.

depositETH(receiver) funds staking using msg.value; deposit(assets,receiver) and mint(shares,receiver) atomically pull WETH from msg.sender and unwrap it. A minimum 0.01 ETH equivalent applies. Shares may be sourced from the configured liquid pool before new minting. Receiver chooses share ownership and must be intentional; use own wallet for own staking. Existing WETH allowance is required but no approval capability is added.

ETH, WETH and spETH use 18-decimal base units. Vendored ERC4626 conversions use virtual assets and shares: shares=floor(assets*(totalSupply+1)/(totalAssets+1)); mint rounds assets up, withdraw rounds burned shares up, redeem rounds assets down. totalAssets uses updater-reported underlying and signed estimated rewards, not a raw onchain balance or backing proof. Share-rate estimates, losses and fees can change; entry methods have no minimum-shares or deadline parameter.

Entry fee is taken from the gross shares before transfer to receiver (except pool caller), so returned/event shares and requested mint shares are gross, not guaranteed receiver-net shares. Admin may set depositFee up to 100 bps and rewardFee up to 2000 bps; current explorer reads depositFee=0 and rewardsFee=500. Whitelist is source-enforced on caller when enabled; current explorer reads whitelistEnabled=false, not a future access promise or jurisdiction/eligibility clearance.

withdraw(assets,receiver,owner) and redeem(shares,receiver,owner) are ASYNCHRONOUS requests, not immediate WETH/ETH payment: burn owner shares, decrease totalUnderlying and queue ETH owed in Withdrawal. If caller differs from owner it consumes owner share allowance. Critically the queue is keyed to caller, NOT owner: use owner=caller for own positions; allowance does not create an owner-keyed claim.

Each new request accumulates caller pending amount, resets unlockEpoch to currentEpoch+1, and OVERWRITES the receiver for the entire accumulated request. Seven-day epochs plus mutable validatorsDisassembleTime determine claim time; current getter reads 604800 seconds, yielding approximately 7–14 days, while source permits up to 90 days additional delay. Current epoch171 exceeds withdrawalsStartEpoch10. No request cancellation, immutable recipient, fixed maturity or validator-exit/liquidity guarantee is asserted.

completeWithdraw() claims only msg.sender pending ledger to its recorded receiver (zero receiver falls back to caller), requires unlock time and sufficient native ETH, decrements totalPendingWithdraw and deletes caller request before sending ETH. Failed receiver payment or insufficient funds reverts. It cannot independently select another claim owner or change receiver.

swapmpETHforETH(amount,minOut) on the documented liquid pool is current spETH FAST unstaking despite legacy method naming: pulls caller spETH under existing allowance and pays native ETH only to caller. minOut bounds net output. Dynamic fee floors spETH amount*feeBps/10000, then converts net shares to ETH; current reads minFee25, maxFee1000, treasuryFee2500 and targetLiquidity21 ETH. Governance may change these; implementation allows maxFee up to1000 and treasury fraction up to7000 bps. Full pre-fee gross ETH must fit tracked pool liquidity; no deadline or guaranteed reserves exists.

Role/admin/upgrades, initializer/recovery distributor, reports and validator activation, signatures, approvals/transfers, pool-only swaps/validator funding, and LP accounting are excluded. Pool LP mint is inherited rather than the staking override and is not admitted. Mutable oracle, validator, treasury, withdrawal and pool behavior remains outside static metadata guarantees.
